name: Emirates NBD
founded: 2007 (incorporated 16 July 2007 following the merger of Emirates Bank International (P.J.S.C.) and National Bank of Dubai (P.J.S.C.))
regulators: UAE CMA (formerly SCA) - Emirates NBD Securities
DFSA - Emirates NBD Asset Management Ltd
ownership_summary: DFM-listed. The H1 2026 financial statements name Investment Corporation of Dubai (ICD), wholly owned by the Government of Dubai, as the Group's parent. Holders above 5% (ownership statistics as at 14 Jul 2026): ICD 40.9%, DH 7 LLC 14.8%, Capital Assets LLC 5.3%; free float 38.8%; foreign ownership 14.4% against a 40% limit. ENBD's 2 Aug 2026 DFM release describes it as 56% owned by the Dubai Government via ICD and Dubai Holding Group.
government_link: Yes - parent is Investment Corporation of Dubai, wholly owned by the Government of Dubai (H1 2026 financial statements, note 1); ENBD states it is 56% owned by the Dubai Government via ICD and Dubai Holding Group (DFM release, 2 Aug 2026).
group_structure: Emirates NBD Bank (P.J.S.C.) is the DFM-listed parent. Main subsidiaries: Emirates Islamic Bank (100% since June 2025; profiled separately as ae-ei - its assets, deposits and profit are consolidated in ENBD's figures, so do not add EI to ENBD totals); DenizBank A.S. (Turkiye, 100%); Emirates NBD Egypt S.A.E. (100%); RBL Bank Ltd (India, 60% acquired and consolidated from 18 Jun 2026, with 40% non-controlling interest); Emirates NBD Asset Management Ltd (DIFC, DFSA-regulated); Emirates NBD Securities LLC (brokerage); Emirates NBD Capital P.S.C., Emirates NBD Capital (KSA) LLC and Emirates NBD Capital India (investment banking / asset management); Emirates NBD Global Services (shared services). Liv is the Group's digital lifestyle bank brand operated by Emirates NBD (captured in this record, not a separate licence). Operating segments: Corporate & Institutional Banking; Retail Banking & Wealth Management (includes private banking, wealth, broking and asset management); Global Markets & Treasury; DenizBank and RBL as separate segments.

footprint: As at Aug 2026 (post-RBL): presence in 13 countries - operations in UAE, Egypt, India, Turkiye, KSA, Singapore, UK, Austria, Germany, Russia and Bahrain, plus representative offices in China and Indonesia; 1,425 branches and 4,948 ATMs/SDMs (DFM release, 2 Aug 2026). International operations contributed ~36% of Group income. Pre-RBL (31 Dec 2025): 787 branches across 13 countries; Emirates Islamic runs 36 UAE branches.
customer_segments: Mass retail; affluent (Priority Banking, with Signature tier by invitation; NRI Priority Banking); private banking (USD 5m+ AUM, UHNW families and family offices); business banking/SME; corporate and institutional (large corporates, multinationals, sovereigns, financial institutions incl. NBFIs, PSPs and asset managers). 25m+ active customers Group-wide as of Aug 2026 incl. RBL Bank.
business_lines: Retail Banking & Wealth Management (cards - #1 issuer in MEA, personal lending, deposits, Priority and Private Banking, wealth management, Emirates NBD Securities brokerage, Emirates NBD Asset Management, consumer finance, Liv digital bank); Corporate & Institutional Banking (lending, transaction banking, trade, investment banking via Emirates NBD Capital - ECM/DCM); Global Markets & Treasury (FX, rates, credit, commodities, structured products); Islamic banking (Emirates Islamic plus Emirates NBD Islamic window); international banking in Turkiye (DenizBank), India (RBL Bank), Egypt, KSA, Singapore and UK.

capabilities.wealth_summary: Wealth sits in Retail Banking & Wealth Management under Marwan Hadi, with a Group-wide AUM figure of USD 105bn at 30 Jun 2026 that explicitly includes assets under administration. Segments run from Priority Banking (AED 500k relationship balance, AED 50k salary or AED 3m home loan) and the invitation-only Signature tier to Private Banking (USD 5m+ AUM) offering advisory, execution, discretionary mandates (via Emirates NBD Asset Management and in-house London private banking), Lombard lending, trust/estate planning and an external asset manager desk. The ENBD X app's Digital Wealth platform (launched Oct 2023) offers 11,000+ global and UAE stocks and ETFs, 232+ mutual funds (ENBD AM, BlackRock, Fidelity, PIMCO with Morningstar ratings), fractional UAE government bonds and sukuk, retail sukuk and Emirates NBD gold; Liv X added crypto trading in Mar 2025 via Aquanow with Zodia custody. In 2025 ENBD added Private Assets Advisory & Execution, partnered with BlackRock for private credit and Shariah-compliant funds, and launched local-currency equity funds and DPM in KSA; digital wealth AUMA almost tripled and trading volumes grew fourfold, and H1 2026 digital wealth trading volumes doubled YoY. Group subsidiaries cover asset management (USD 16bn AUM, DIFC/Jersey/Luxembourg/Cayman funds), brokerage (Emirates NBD Securities: DFM, ADX, Nasdaq Dubai, Tadawul) and investment banking (Emirates NBD Capital).

segments.name: Priority Banking
segments.eligibility: Any one of: monthly salary AED 50,000+; home loan AED 3m+; deposits and/or investments AED 500,000+. Salary/home-loan entrants must build and maintain AED 500,000 total relationship balance within 12 months.

segments.name: Signature (by Priority Banking)
segments.eligibility: By invitation only, for the 'upper crust' of Priority Banking clientele; offers advisory, execution, Lombard lending, offshore booking centres, trust & estate planning (no published threshold).

segments.name: Private Banking
segments.eligibility: USD 5 million (or equivalent) and above in AUM with the bank (held by client, family or business).

private_banking.detail: Emirates NBD Private Banking (Group Head: Mohammad Al Bastaki). Threshold USD 5m AUM. Services: investment advisory, trade execution (equities, fixed income, futures, commodities, FX), discretionary portfolio management (via Emirates NBD Asset Management and in-house Private Banking in London), Lombard and real-estate lending incl. IPO financing, trust & estate planning, real estate advisory (UAE and Prime Central London), External Asset Management desk in Dubai, Next Gen programme (with PwC, INSEAD). Strategic agreement with DIFC Family Wealth Centre for UHNW families (3 Dec 2025). Awards: FT Best Private Bank 2025; Euromoney Private Banking. Platforms strengthened in Singapore and UK; onshore derivatives and structured investments activated in Singapore (2025).

asset_management.detail: Emirates NBD Asset Management Ltd (DIFC, DFSA-regulated; SEO Michail Samawi): AUM USD 16bn at 31 Mar 2026. Funds domiciled in DIFC (FundStar umbrella), Jersey, Luxembourg (Emirates NBD SICAV) and Cayman: MENA equities, fixed income/EM debt, global multi-asset, money market, Shariah-compliant funds (e.g. Emirates Global Sukuk Fund, Emirates Islamic Money Market Fund, Emirates Islamic Global Balanced Fund), CIO Signature Funds; segregated discretionary/non-discretionary mandates; ENBD REIT (Shariah-compliant, Nasdaq Dubai); co-managed funds with Jupiter AM and UTI International. Group third-party funds managed AED 72.6bn (31 Dec 2025). Also Emirates NBD Capital India (asset management) and KSA local-currency equity funds/DPM launched 2025.

brokerage.detail: Emirates NBD Securities LLC (licensed by UAE Capital Market Authority, licence 604003): DFM, ADX, Nasdaq Dubai and Saudi Exchange (Tadawul) plus GCC markets; channels Securities Online, eBrokerMax and the Emirates NBD Securities app with digital account opening. Digital margin trading facility enhanced with higher limits (H1 2026). 2026 priority: 'most comprehensive access to GCC & presence country markets on Emirates NBD Securities'. Global equities brokerage is offered in-app via ENBD X Digital Wealth. (UAE SCA was reconstituted as the Capital Market Authority from 1 Jan 2026 per law-firm briefing, search result only.)

digital_investing.detail: ENBD X Digital Wealth (launched Oct 2023): 11,000+ global and UAE stocks and ETFs (NYSE, Nasdaq, LSE, DFM, ADX, Nasdaq Dubai); 232+ mutual funds (from Jan 2024); fractional UAE government bonds and sukuk and GCC sovereign fixed income (2025); retail sukuk; Emirates NBD gold; no minimum balance; zero brokerage on DFM/ADX/Nasdaq Dubai and USD 2 minimum fee on global equities/ETFs (FAQ). ENBD X launched in KSA in 2025 and is planned for Egypt in 2026. Liv X (Liv digital bank) offers crypto trading since Mar 2025. Rewards Hub on ENBD X (H1 2026). Digital wealth AUMA almost tripled in 2025; trading volumes >AED 40bn in 2025 and doubled YoY in H1 2026.

discrepancies.detail: Batch brief describes Emirates Islamic as DFM-listed; ENBD FY2025 financial statements (note 47) state ENBD acquired the remaining 0.1% and EI 'has been de-listed from Dubai Financial Markets'; EI's own FY2025 statements give trading suspension on 10 Jun 2025.

discrepancies.resolution: Recorded 2.4m with status 'Conflicting sources'; scope difference (Group vs UAE retail) likely but not stated.

discrepancies.detail: Strategic Report shows '9.8+mn' total active customers and elsewhere 'Over 9 million active customers'.
discrepancies.resolution: Used 9.8m (more specific); both consistent as floors.

discrepancies.detail: Entrepreneur ME (28 Jul 2026) body says he 'served as Group CEO of Emirates NBD for 12 years' (past tense) while headline and caption title him Group CEO.
discrepancies.resolution: Official management page (12 Oct 2026) and DFM release (2 Aug 2026) list him as Group CEO; treated as wording, role 'Verified current'.

discrepancies.detail: ENBD AM 'About us' (undated) lists Tariq Mushtaq Chaudhary as 'Group Head of Wealth Management' and Mohammad Al Bastaki as 'Group Head of Private Banking'; Caproasia (18 Dec 2025) reports Chaudhary moved to Group Head RBWM International, Raed Al Jaser named Head of Wealth Management and Al Bastaki Group Head of Private Banking & Wealth Management; ENBD release (3 Dec 2025) uses 'Group Head of Private Banking and Wealth Management' for Al Bastaki. Re-read 2026-10-12: the ENBD AM bio for Chaudhary dates itself to about 2023 ('joined his current position earlier this year', 'the last nine years' since 2014), so the page is stale rather than a current contradiction, but no official 2025-2026 source confirms the Caproasia titles.
discrepancies.resolution: Al Bastaki title taken from the official 3 Dec 2025 release; Chaudhary 'Conflicting sources' (appointed 2025 per report, no effective date); Al Jaser 'Requires verification'.

discrepancies.detail: Jan 2024 ENBD release names Pedro Sousa Cardoso as Chief Digital Officer, RBWM; FinTech Futures headlines (search results only, page blocked) report he stepped down and joined ADCB as CDO (around Oct 2025).
discrepancies.resolution: Not listed as a current person; successor for RBWM digital not identified (open item).

discrepancies.detail: ENBD CG Report 2025 gives 'Year appointed: 1991'; EI Annual Report 2025 gives 'Year joined: 2006'; EI's 5 Sep 2023 appointment release cites a 'thirty-two-year industry track record' (consistent with 1991 as an industry start date). The 2023 release styles his previous post 'Head of Consumer Banking and Wealth Management'; CG Report and EI AR say 'Head of Retail Banking and Wealth Management'.
